How this supports improvement Reveals recurring gaps in access control or watchkeeping Supports reinforcement of proper security practices through visibility Enables comparison across vessels without losing operational context Strengthens onboard security culture through consistent follow-up Clarity During Elevated Security Situations The Security Module provides additional context when security risk is heightened. Where this matters most Port calls and cargo operations Gangway and access management during crew changes Navigation through higher-risk areas Reviews following suspicious activity or security alerts Operational Context That Drives Action Across the Fleet Insights from the Security Module are combined with signals from across the fleet, providing a consistent view of how security practices are implemented across vessels, ports, and voyages. This shared context helps teams identify where attention is needed, prioritize follow-up, and maintain alignment from ship to shore. Explore Fleetvision Who This Is For Masters & Senior Officers Maintain safer operations with better situational awareness. Clear, real-time visibility into how vessel security is maintained during everyday operations, supporting consistent access control, disciplined watchkeeping, and confident decision-making when conditions change. QHSE & Risk Leaders Move from reactive reporting to proactive safety. Fleet-wide insight into how security procedures are executed across vessels, enabling earlier engagement, targeted assessments, and more effective prevention before risks escalate. Fleet Managers & Operations Operate the fleet with one clear, consistent view of risk. A consolidated view of security execution across the fleet that helps identify exposure patterns, prioritize follow-up during port calls or higher-risk transits, and maintain consistent security standards. Why This Matters FleetVision shifts security management from incident response to continuous operational awareness, helping reduce exposure, prevent breaches, and maintain confidence across the fleet. Book a demo FAQ Is the Security Module intended to monitor individual crew members? No. The Security Module focuses on operational execution and access control, not individual surveillance or enforcement. Does FleetVision replace the vessel security plan or ISPS procedures? No. It complements existing security frameworks by adding day-to-day visibility between audits, drills, and incidents. How are security alerts used in practice? Alerts draw attention to conditions or activity that may require clarification or response. How teams act on them is defined by the operator’s existing security procedures. Who controls access to security footage and data? All access is controlled by the operator and aligned with established roles, permissions, and governance policies. jobs.title: About Us Redefining how maritime risk is controlled
jobs.description: About ShipIn | The Maritime Fleet Safety AI Company Solutions Safety & Risk Detect early risk signals before they escalate Security Protect vessels, crews, and operations Efficiency Improve performance across daily operations Product FleetVision Platform Turn operational insight into fleet-wide action Bridge Correct navigation drift before incidents Technical Act on failure signals before downtime MARPOL Address compliance gaps before findings Safety Intervene on unsafe behavior in real time Security Respond to threats before breaches escalate Cargo Soon Request early access for future deployment Insights Insights Maritime Industry Insights & Analysis Blog Perspectives on risk, safety, and performance White Papers Deep analysis of maritime risk and prevention News & Events Announcements, partnerships, and global events Company About Us Redefining how maritime risk is controlled Careers Join us in reshaping maritime safety Log In Book a Demo Log In Book a Demo ShipIn by the numbers 1,500 + vessels supported worldwide 2.5 B+ hours of onboard operational activity analyzed 35 % of worlds largest fleet companies use ShipIn 40 % reduction in onboard incidents observed in deployments What We Believe Safe operations depend on understanding how work unfolds onboard vessels. Incidents rarely begin with a single failure. They develop over time through small signals and conditions that often go unnoticed. For decades, most insight has come after an incident through reports and investigations. While important, they provide clarity only after something has already gone wrong. ShipIn was built for seafarers by seafarers, based on the belief that crews and shore teams need better visibility into daily operations to recognize risks earlier and address them before they escalate Our Mission ShipIn is the defining intelligence platform for maritime operations, trusted by operators, recognized by regulators, and valued for turning operational complexity and risk into clear, actionable insight. Beyond building powerful technology, we aim to help shape the future standard of safety, visibility, and operational effectiveness across global shipping. Leadership ShipIn is led by a team with deep experience across maritime operations, artificial intelligence, and enterprise technology. Together, the leadership team is focused on helping the shipping industry better understand operational risk and improve safety across global fleets. Osher Perry Founder & Chief Executive Officer Osher Perry founded ShipIn to bring greater operational visibility to maritime organizations. With a background spanning naval service, maritime operations, and technology entrepreneurship, he recognized the need for better insight into daily vessel operations once ships leave port. Under his leadership, ShipIn developed the FleetVision platform, transforming onboard cameras into a source of operational intelligence for fleets around the world. Daniela Krispin Chief Technology Officer Daniela Krispin leads ShipIn’s technology and engineering organization. She brings more than two decades of experience building large-scale data platforms, AI systems, and enterprise software. At ShipIn, she oversees the development of the FleetVision platform and the company’s advanced computer vision and data infrastructure. Ahmed Khan Chief Customer Officer Captain Ahmed Khan is a Master Mariner with more than two decades of experience in maritime operations and fleet management. He leads ShipIn’s global customer organization, working closely with shipowners and operators to ensure successful deployment and operational impact across fleets. Gal Sagy Chief Revenue Officer Gal Sagy leads ShipIn’s global commercial organization. With a background in enterprise technology and startup leadership, he is responsible for the company’s growth strategy, partnerships, and expansion across the global maritime industry. Nadav Cohen Chief Product Officer Nadav Cohen leads product strategy and development for the FleetVision platform. He brings extensive experience building enterprise software and data-driven products, with a focus on translating complex operational environments into intuitive, scalable platforms. Adi Golani Chief of Staff Adi Golani supports organizational strategy and execution across ShipIn. She works closely with the executive team to coordinate key initiatives, drive cross-functional alignment, and support the company’s continued global growth. Advisory Board ShipIn’s advisory board brings deep expertise from across the maritime, regulatory, and technology sectors. Their guidance helps ensure the company’s technology aligns with the operational realities of global shipping and supports safer, more transparent maritime operations. Kirsi Tikka Advisory Board Dr. Kirsi Tikka is a globally recognized leader in maritime safety, classification, and regulatory development. During her tenure at the American Bureau of Shipping, she oversaw global engineering and regulatory affairs, helping shape safety standards and technological innovation across the shipping industry. Her decades of experience working with shipowners, regulators, and classification societies provide valuable insight as ShipIn works to advance operational visibility and risk management across fleets. Scott Armour Advisory Board Scott Armour brings extensive experience in enterprise technology and global business leadership. During his time at Oracle, he held senior executive roles focused on scaling enterprise software platforms and leading international sales and operations. His experience building and scaling global technology organizations supports ShipIn’s mission to deliver advanced operational intelligence solutions to the maritime industry. View open roles Meet the team Why ShipIn Built by seafarers for seafarers ShipIn was founded by people who understand what it’s like to operate vessels at sea. We build technology that supports crews and operators in real conditions, not systems designed only in a lab. Committed to the people and industry we serve ShipIn operates as a Public Benefit Corporation. That means we are committed to improving safety and transparency across maritime operations while building a company that serves shipowners, crews, and the broader industry. Driven by innovation at sea ShipIn is building a new category of maritime technology. By combining AI, computer vision, and deep operational insight, we are tackling challenges that have never been solved before. The complexity of what we build makes the work here deeply engaging, requiring creativity, curiosity, and the courage to think beyond conventional solutions. Open Positions Don’t See the Right Role for You? Send Us Your Resume. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We’re always looking for talent. If you do not see the right maritime industry job opening for you, but are still interested in joining us to transform Maritime Shipping, please send your resume to careers@shipin.ai . Why Now The maritime industry is entering a new phase where operational visibility and safety intelligence are becoming essential. ShipIn is helping define this category, with deployments on thousands of vessels and billions of hours of real-world operational data. We are still early in building the platform fleets will rely on to understand and manage operational risk at sea, so there is much to build from the ground up. Our Values Crew-first A strong ship depends on its crew. We treat each other with respect, support one another, and create an environment where people can thrive. Always growing We get better by doing. Challenges are not obstacles - they’re how we learn. We step outside our comfort zone, try new things, and improve with every step. Own the ship We take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks. When something isn’t working, we don’t wait - we step in, fix it, and make sure things move forward. One crew We succeed together. We share knowledge, communicate openly, and support each other to move faster and make better decisions. Trust is the product Accuracy, transparency, and reliability are non-negotiable. If we lose trust, we lose everything. Benefits and support Building technology that improves safety at sea is serious work. We want ShipIn to be a place where people can do meaningful work while being supported in their careers and lives.
